message:
Params via Go 1.7 Contexts (#147)

* Supports Params in net/http Handlers with go1.7+

Go 1.7 introduces request-scoped context, providing a place to hang
Params even in net/http standard Handlers attached with Router.Handler
or Router.HandlerFunc.

This provides an alternative implementation of Router.Handler which
attaches the params to the request context. It also includes a bit of
new public API: ParamsKey is the context key used, and
ParamsFromContext uses ParamsKey to get Params from a context.Context.

All of this is guarded by a "go1.7" build tag. With go 1.6 and older
none of the new API is available and Params continue to be thrown away
in Handler/HandlerFunc-attached endpoints.

* WithValue is the 'context' function

* use an un-exported struct{} alias to collision-proof the key

* no longer a const

* update README.md to reflect additional allocations with the stdlib-compatible api

pr.title: Params via Go 1.7 Contexts
pr.body:
With request-scoped contexts coming to `net/http` in go 1.7 there's no need for `Handler` and `HandlerFunc` to continue throwing away `Params`.

It may be a little early for this change, but I wanted to get your eyes on it and start the discussion.

 **Parameters in your routing pattern:** Stop parsing the requested URL path, just give the path segment a name and the router delivers the dynamic value to you. Because of the design of the router, path parameters are very cheap.
 
-**Zero Garbage:** The matching and dispatching process generates zero bytes of garbage. In fact, the only heap allocations that are made, is by building the slice of the key-value pairs for path parameters. If the request path contains no parameters, not a single heap allocation is necessary.
+**Zero Garbage:** The matching and dispatching process generates zero bytes of garbage. The only heap allocations that are made are building the slice of the key-value pairs for path parameters, and building new context and request objects (the latter only in the standard `Handler`/`HandlerFunc` api). In the 3-argument API, if the request path contains no parameters not a single heap allocation is necessary.
 
 **Best Performance:** [Benchmarks speak for themselves](https://github.com/julienschmidt/go-http-routing-benchmark). See below for technical details of the implementation.

+
+package httprouter
+
+import "net/http"
+
+// Handler is an adapter which allows the usage of an http.Handler as a
+// request handle. With go 1.7+, the Params will be available in the
+// request context under ParamsKey.
+func (r *Router) Handler(method, path string, handler http.Handler) {
+	r.Handle(method, path,
+		func(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request, _ Params) {
+			handler.ServeHTTP(w, req)
+		},
+	)
+}

diff --git a/stdparams.go b/stdparams.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..abb4209
--- /dev/null
+++ b/stdparams.go
@@ -0,0 +1,38 @@
+// +build go1.7
+
+package httprouter
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"net/http"
+)
+
+type paramsKey struct{}
+
+// ParamsKey is the request context key under which URL params are stored.
+//
+// This is only present from go 1.7.
+var ParamsKey = paramsKey{}
+
+// Handler is an adapter which allows the usage of an http.Handler as a
+// request handle. With go 1.7+, the Params will be available in the
+// request context under ParamsKey.
+func (r *Router) Handler(method, path string, handler http.Handler) {
+	r.Handle(method, path,
+		func(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request, p Params) {
+			ctx := req.Context()
+			ctx = context.WithValue(ctx, ParamsKey, p)
+			req = req.WithContext(ctx)
+			handler.ServeHTTP(w, req)
+		},
+	)
+}
+
+// ParamsFromContext pulls the URL parameters from a request context,
+// or returns nil if none are present.
+//
+// This is only present from go 1.7.
+func ParamsFromContext(ctx context.Context) Params {
+	p, _ := ctx.Value(ParamsKey).(Params)
+	return p
+}

explanation.what: 標準の http.Handler / http.HandlerFunc アダプタ経由でも Params にアクセスできるようにした。go1.7 ビルドタグ付きの stdparams.go を新設し、Router.Handler の実装を「Params を context.WithValue で request context に載せてから handler.ServeHTTP を呼ぶ」形に置き換え、context から取り出すための ParamsKey と ParamsFromContext を公開した。go1.6 以前向けには、Params を単に捨てる従来実装を nonstdparams.go(!go1.7 ビルドタグ)に退避して router.go から削除した。
explanation.why: PR本文にある通り、Go 1.7 で net/http にリクエストスコープの context が入ったことで、Handler/HandlerFunc に登録したハンドラでも Params を捨てずに渡せるようになったため。これまで3引数の独自 Handle シグネチャ(w, req, Params)を使わない標準 http.Handler ルートでは Params が失われていたが、この変更でその制約を解消した。ビルドタグで新旧2実装を切り替えることで、Go 1.6 以前のユーザーへの後方互換を保っている。

highlights.note: context.WithValue → req.WithContext → handler.ServeHTTP という Params 引き渡しの核心部分
旧 Router.Handler 実装を削除し、ビルドタグ別ファイルに委譲した箇所

langNotes.note: Go 1.7 で net/http にリクエストスコープの context.Context が標準搭載された。context.WithValue(ctx, key, value) で値を持つ新しい Context を作り、req.WithContext(ctx) で Request に付け替えるのが定石。ここでは衝突を避けるため、空 struct 型 paramsKey{} を非公開のキー型として使っている(文字列キーだと他パッケージの同名キーと衝突しうるため)。
ファイル先頭のビルドタグコメントで、コンパイル対象の Go バージョンによって参照するファイルを切り替えている。stdparams.go は go1.7 以上でのみ、nonstdparams.go はそれ未満でのみビルドされ、同名関数 Router.Handler の実装がバージョンごとに1つだけ解決される。

diagram.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant R as "Router.Handler adapter"
  participant Ctx as "context.Context"
  participant H as "http.Handler"
  R->>Ctx: "context.WithValue(ParamsKey, Params)"
  R->>R: "req.WithContext(ctx)"
  R->>H: "handler.ServeHTTP(w, req)"
  H->>Ctx: "ParamsFromContext(req.Context())"
  Ctx-->>H: "Params"
diagram.caption: 標準 http.Handler アダプタが Params を context 経由で受け渡す流れ
